note: STD-537. The authoritative machine-readable form of the typed source-selection vectors of TC-935 (FR-330-AC-10). `selections` are exact FR-322 `Selection` rows; the short labels T, D and U denote these typed values, never identifier-parsing rules. `compatibility_cases` give, per TC-935 table case, the `expected` result text and the `required_source_selections` and the input `lock.profile_selections` as lists of labels, in order; `repeat_controls` are the sentences of the TC-935 paragraph that begins "Repeat the unrelated case", verbatim and in order. A consumer reads this file (for example through QUIRE_SPECIFICATION_DIR) and never copies or redefines the rows; the QSpec test asserts they equal the fenced JSON block and table of spec/test-cases/TC-935-contract-package-profile.md.

compatibility_cases.expected: Both requested items lower; source lock and package equal that input exactly.
Exactly `invalid_input(b)`, `invalid_input(a)`; no semantic nodes; both exact request occurrence sets retained.
The same two `invalid_input` records; no substitute `T`, no node or backend artifact; output still retains `[D]` and its originating package.
Both items lower; output retains `[U, T]` in that order, including the unrelated row.

repeat_controls: Repeat the unrelated case with lock order `[T, U]` in a separately admitted package: compatibility remains true and the output preserves that input's own order/id, rather than equating the two package identities.
Repeat with requirements `[T, T]` and `[U, T]`/`[T, U]`: duplicate and order changes do not change compatibility.
With requirements `[T, D]`, lock `[T]` refuses and an independently admitted lock containing both rows matches.
Repeat a mismatch with only an unrelated row `[U]` to prove it cannot satisfy `T`.
With requirements `[]`, the `[D]` input lowers without inferred requirements or lock repair.

For a same-identity/different-authority control, require the `T` row with only its authority changed to `other-authority`; the original `[T]` input refuses rather than matching its display identity alone.
In every refusal, the serialized record has only `node_id` and `disposition: "invalid_input"`; no fabricated cause/pointer is added.
Compare the entire emitted source lock and originating package against the retained expected values on every successful and refused run, not merely the row used by the predicate.
These are producer controls; the ContractPackage reader is not given or assumed to reconstruct requirements.
